raw: #1: = ♦ Τον ἀρτον ἡμων τον ἐπιουσιον διδου ἡμιν το καθ᾽ ἡμεραν. There has been considerable diversity of opinion as to the precise meaning of the word ἐπιουσιον. As the idea of "daily" is fully expressed by the phrase καθ᾽ ἡμεραν, it seems probable that the word ἐπιουσιον is intended to express something different. The idea that this is a petition for the bread of "to-morrow," though adopted by Lightfoot, is surely untenable and paradoxical. Origen says that the word ἐπιουσιος seems to have been formed by the evangelists; as it does not occur in any of the earlier Greek writers—ἐοικε πεπλασθαι ὑπο των εὐαγγελιστων: he renders the word, however, ἐφημερον, "daily;" as does also Chrysostom. I adhere to the opinion of those who think the word is intended to signify "sufficient," or, sufficient for subsistence: *quasi* ἐπι οὐσιαν. As περιουσιος signifies abundant, ἐπιουσιος seems to signify sufficient. This explanation of the word is given by Theophylact: Ἀρτος ἐπι τῃ οὐσιᾳ και συστασι ἡμων αὐταρκη, "bread sufficient for our subsistence, and sustenance."
